text:
Take random-order binding at rapid equilibrium: E + A ⇌ E(A) (K1), E + B ⇌ E(B) (K2), E(A) + B ⇌ E(A, B) (K3), E(B) + A ⇌ E(A, B) (K4). An equilibrium exists only if both routes to E(A, B) agree: K1·K3 = K2·K4.

In AllParameters, with no thermodynamic relations, all four constants are free. The derivation computes the equilibrium weights along one spanning tree of the segment (route through E(A) or through E(B)), so the constant that closes the loop never enters v: it is listed as a parameter but has no effect. Which one is dropped depends on the order the steps are stored in, which in 23 mechanisms changes the AllParameters law.

The fix imposes only the relations of cycles made entirely of rapid-equilibrium steps, in every mode. That is part of the rapid-equilibrium assumption, not thermodynamics applied to rate constants. Cycles that contain a steady-state step stay unconstrained in AllParameters.

Follow-up: yes. Full mode prints today's Reduced v line with the dependent lines removed and every listed constant read from params. Inside each rapid-equilibrium segment that v line multiplies the K's along one breadth-first spanning tree, so the K that closes an RE loop never appears in it. In Reduced mode that K still reaches v, because a Wegscheider line computes a tree K from it. Full mode drops that line, so the K is listed and ignored.

Example, expand_bibi/265: E + A ⇌ E(A); E + B ⇌ E(B); E(A) + B ⇌ E(A, B); E(B) + A ⇌ E(A, B); E(A, B) <--> E(P, Q); E(P, Q) ⇌ E(P) + Q; E(P) ⇌ E + P. Full mode lists K_EAB_to_EB_A (A binding to E(B)), but v contains only the route through E(A).

- Writing the steps in another order changes nothing: the constructor sorts them.
- Names decide the tree. E(A) sorts before E(B), so the route through E(A) wins. Rename A to Z and the route through E(B) wins, so B binding to E(A) is the constant dropped instead.
- With K(A|EB) = 4, where the loop requires 1.5, Full mode gives v = 1.315 under one naming and 0.515 under the other. Raising the ignored constant to 1e6 leaves v unchanged.

Of the 27 mechanisms with such a loop, 23 drop a listed K this way (21 of them enumerated). In 3 specs the single-symbol tie closes the loop without saying so; in 1 the loop's relation is simply missing.

Steady-state loops are different: every rate constant appears in the steady-state law, so Full mode is complete there, and constants that break detailed balance only make flux circulate. That is why the fix imposes the relations of loops made entirely of RE steps and nothing else.

Follow-up: agreed, and it settles this card. With one law in independent parameters there is no Full-mode derivation to repair: an RE loop gets its dependent K from the joint solve, as Reduced mode does today.

What goes:

- the Full and Reduced exports, the mode types, and the three Full methods of parameters, rate_equation and rate_equation_string;
- the Full-mode section of the textbook docs page and about 15 test lines that use Full mode;
- two D1 bugs, the open RE loop and the Pass-2 fold in Full mode.

What stays:

- parameters(m): the independent constants plus Keq and E_total, today's default, now without a mode argument;
- fitted_params(m): the fitted subset;
- all_parameters(m, params): every constant of every step, with the dependents computed from the independent values. It replaces the test helper that reaches into the derivation's internals today.

One point on direction: the tests need independent to all. They draw independent values, fill in the dependents and compare the textbook formula with rate_equation. The reverse, all constants to independent ones, only picks names, and it is right only when the constants already obey Haldane and Wegscheider.

What is lost is evaluating a textbook law at constants that break Haldane, which you have accepted. I added this as an option on the card.
